data.description:
China's memory-chip company, CXMT, has garnered interest from tech giants like Apple Inc. for its advanced chips, though this growth has made it a target in the US-China tech conflict. Pentagon blacklisted CXMT over alleged military ties, while former Samsung employees were accused of leaking information to CXMT. US officials closely monitor CXMT's expansion to prevent Chinese semiconductor access to advanced technology.

CXMT's success hinges on narrowing the tech gap with industry leaders like Samsung and avoiding severe restrictions that could disrupt its supply chain. CXMT's journey began in 2017 with its first factory in Hefei as another Chinese chip project, sFujian Jinhua, faced US pressure. Jinhua's downfall benefited CXMT, securing funding and teaching the company to navigate US policy boundaries.

Washington's export controls in 2022 restricted high-end chips, equipment, and expertise to impede China's tech progress. Despite limitations in accessing cutting-edge technology, CXMT showcased its first 12-inch DRAM memory wafers at the 2024 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei. The company's focus on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) crucial for AI infrastructure challenges dominant players like Samsung and Micron.

CXMT aims to reduce US dependency by building a Chinese-centered supply chain, aligning with Beijing's tech self-sufficiency push. Ranked fourth in the global memory-chip market, CXMT trails industry leaders but disrupts the three-company dominance. A planned $4.4 billion IPO aims to boost technology and R&D, aligning with China's tech ambitions.

Memory chips are vital for AI systems, positioning the US and China as key players fueling tech growth. CXMT benefits from China's restrictions on Micron, offering a local alternative amid limited global suppliers. Founder Zhu Yiming's background in the US and China tech sectors influences CXMT's trajectory.

Zhu's experience from GigaDevice to CXMT shapes the company's commercial and technical foundation. CXMT symbolizes contrasting strategies for Beijing and Washington. China sees it as proof of national financing and policy success, while the US grapples with export controls' impact on China's tech rise.

CXMT's growing prominence invites opportunities like Apple's interest but also risks from geopolitical tensions and security concerns. CXMT doesn't need to surpass industry leaders to impact the global market. Establishing a reliable Chinese memory-chip source reduces Beijing's foreign reliance, boosts domestic suppliers, and diminishes US leverage.

CXMT's journey underscores the complex interplay between technology, geopolitics, and economic power. Photographer: Li Xukui/NBD/VCG/Getty Images
